How to Contact These Brands (Beyond Just Filling a Form)

Application forms are convenient, but they're not always the most effective way to get PR packages. Here's why email outreach often works better:

Why Email Outreach Beats Application Forms

  • Forms get buried: Popular brands receive hundreds of applications weekly. Your form submission sits in a queue with everyone else.
  • Email stands out: A well-crafted email lands directly in someone's inbox. It's personal, shows effort, and demonstrates professionalism.
  • You control the narrative: Forms ask for what brands want to know. Email lets you highlight what makes you valuable.
  • Faster responses: Email pitches typically get responses within 3-7 days. Form applications can take 4-6 weeks (if they respond at all).

The Anatomy of a PR Pitch Email That Gets Replies

For ready-to-use templates, see our 5 copy-paste brand pitch email templates for small creators. Here's what every pitch email should include:

  1. Specific product mention: Name something you love about their brand. Generic "I love your products" gets deleted.
  2. Your numbers: Follower count, engagement rate, and audience demographics (age, location, interests).
  3. Content proposal: Exactly what content you'd create. "I'll make a post" is weak. "I'll create a 60-second unboxing Reel showing my morning routine" is strong.
  4. Your media kit: Attached as a PDF. This should include your best work, audience insights, and past brand collaborations.

What Brands Look For Before Sending PR

Before you apply, make sure you have these basics covered:

  • Consistent posting: At least 3-4 posts per week shows you're active and reliable.
  • Engagement over followers: 3-6% engagement rate matters more than follower count. Brands know this.
  • Niche alignment: A skincare brand won't send PR to a gaming creator. Be clear about your niche.
  • Quality content: Your last 9 posts are your portfolio. Make sure they showcase your best work.
  • Professional presence: Clear bio, professional email, and a media kit ready to share.

Need help creating a media kit? Check our guide on how to create a media kit in under 30 minutes.

FAQ

How many followers do I need to get PR packages?

Most brands work with creators starting at 1,000-5,000 followers. Some brands like COSRX and Tower 28 accept creators with as few as 1K followers. Focus on engagement rate (3%+) rather than follower count — brands increasingly prioritize engagement over raw numbers. newcollab connects creators of all sizes with brands actively seeking authentic partnerships.

Do I need to post about every PR package I receive?

It depends on the brand's terms. Some send "no-strings" gifting where posting is appreciated but not required. Others have structured programs requiring 1-3 posts per package. Always clarify expectations before accepting. Read the agreement carefully or ask directly.

How long does it take to hear back from brands?

Application forms: 2-6 weeks (many don't respond at all). Direct email pitches: 3-10 days. Follow up after 7 days if you haven't heard back — a polite follow-up email often gets responses that the initial pitch didn't.

Can PR packages lead to paid collaborations?

Yes, frequently. Brands use PR seeding to test creators before investing in paid partnerships. Deliver excellent content on your PR posts, share performance metrics with the brand, and many will offer paid work within 3-6 months. 63% of creators on newcollab report receiving paid offers after successful PR collaborations.
